productionSourceDiff.interpretation: No production-code changes since ec0d0a0; HEAD adds retained evidence and documentation only.

scope.purpose: Finite exhaustive audit boundary for built-in supported operational consumers and writer roles, with concrete remaining evidence controls.
supportedPublicSurfaces: transport-neutral command runtime and command definitions
MCP command tools and integration resources
finiteBuiltInBoundary: 115 CLI command definitions and their 115 canonical executors
all built-in command implementations, storage boundary/admission modules, validators, bundle/export/import code, and checked-in CI/examples/conformance/documentation consumers named by the plan
literal filesystem role inventory and import-bound atomic writer inventory as discovery inputs, with transitive ownership still requiring behavior/source evidence
explicitLimits: A trusted raw node:sqlite DatabaseSync caller can deliberately rewrite a local database; the low-level helper cannot infer target identity and this is outside the package root/./integration/MCP supported actor boundary.
Privileged or third-party processes can produce filesystem side effects; the plan requires supported-client admission and old-client exclusion, not universal prevention of unknown processes.

Portable exports, bundle/signing output, installation/configuration, repository-index/search transport and external evidence scratch are explicit file-owned surfaces when their destination and authority are reviewed; they are not operational SQLite authority.
Static inventories do not prove dynamic aliases, assigned callbacks, dependency internals, arbitrary parameters or every external process effect.

transportAndPathFamilies: CLI argument parsing and command runtime
MCP tool registry, resource registry and server transport
bundle generation and portable export/import/attachment digest boundaries
CI workflows, examples, conformance fixtures and documentation references

fixedRegressionInterpretation.note: Do not reopen the historical continuity/bundle defect preparation as an unresolved production defect; the retained current receipt records the ten controls as passed.

supportedChain.claim: Validates input, resolves target and invokes canonical executor with authority/runtime context outside actor-controlled input.
Routes ordinary commands through project storage and storage exceptions through dedicated admission; backup uses admitted source.
Supported ./integration surface re-exports canonical command/resource APIs.
MCP tools derive metadata, strip actor authority/runtime fields, apply policy and delegate to canonical command runtime.
MCP/integration resource reads use read-only project storage snapshots.
Public backup admits source store for target, constrains destination and passes admitted db/target to backup service.
Operational context target mismatch fails closed.
Canonical admission handles maintenance/legacy locks, fresh SQLite bootstrap, mixed legacy refusal and project admission.
SQLite path/device/inode/root/sidecar identity is checked before reuse.

lowLevelContract.conclusion: No public target-misbinding defect was found; no regression should be manufactured for the trusted low-level helper contract.

exporter.contract: exportTask/exportDatabase receive authoritative db, task/destination and optional attachmentRoot from a trusted caller; attachment bytes are size/digest verified. They do not infer a source target.

projectBackup.contract: backupProjectStorage receives admitted db/target/destination and binds database plus attachment inventory before publication.

lowLevelContract.publicBoundary: The public command calls getOperationalStore(target), validates a safe destination and passes the admitted store/target. A raw DatabaseSync caller remains outside the supported public boundary.

notRemainingDefects: The prepared continuity and portable bundle identity defects are not current unresolved regressions; the current ec0 receipt records the ten prepared controls as passed.
No public exporter/backup target-misbinding defect was found under the supported authority chain.
No concrete built-in normal-operation legacy filesystem writer was identified in the finite supported boundary; existing controls refuse named legacy/mixed/missing-state fallback cases.
Universal prevention of deliberate raw DatabaseSync rewrites or privileged external filesystem changes is outside the declared supported-client threat boundary.
